acceptance_criteria: BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT requests plan deterministically to approved archive objects.
UTC daily/monthly caller and source-object boundaries are tested.
Only the approved public Binance source is used without API credentials.
Checksum mismatch and malformed archive never produce a completed artifact.
Raw Parquet preserves complete contract-Kline source semantics.
Successful objects are persisted through shared Raw store manifests.
Existing, missing, checksum/parse, and local/conflict outcomes remain distinct.
Partial multi-object runs are not reported complete and do not destroy successful immutable objects.
Controlled local fixtures cover success, checksum failure, invalid archive, and a cross-boundary request.
No mark/index/funding, REST sync/repair, canonical quality repair, feature, backtest, or trading capability is included.

critical_outcome.capability: Backfill BTCUSDT 1m contract Kline from an approved archive through checksum, parser, and Raw store
critical_outcome.observable_result: Source objects have explicit outcomes and completed artifacts can be revalidated; corrupt input cannot publish a completed object

requirements: Use the completed Research archive source, publication, time-boundary, checksum, and source-selection decisions.
Use the public-history request/source contract and shared Raw persistence API; do not create a second object identity or manifest format.
Support only the Binance USDⓈ-M 1m contract-Kline archive path for BTCUSDT and ETHUSDT.
Plan arbitrary timezone-aware UTC [start, end) requests into deterministic daily/monthly source-object boundaries.
Keep not-found, retryable transport/server failure, invalid content, and local failure distinct.
Verify an available upstream checksum before publishing a completed Raw artifact.
Validate ZIP structure, CSV shape, headers, row timestamps, and basic format completeness.
Preserve the complete Binance wire-schema Raw fields without canonical renaming, fill, dedupe, repair, or aggregation.
Use Raw store reconciliation for existing objects and immutable content conflicts.

Use controlled local HTTP/archive fixtures and cover a request crossing a source-object boundary.

No REST recent synchronization or gap repair.
